reading.title: The Secret Language of Whales
reading.text: Whales are known for their complex vocalisations, often called songs. Humpback whales, in particular, produce long, melodic sequences that can travel hundreds of kilometers underwater. Scientists have discovered that these songs follow grammatical rules similar to human languages. Each song is composed of themes and phrases that repeat in a specific order. Whales may use songs to attract mates, navigate, or maintain social bonds. Interestingly, whale songs evolve over time; a tune heard one year may be completely different the next, suggesting cultural transmission among pods.

reading.title: The Pyramids: Ancient Engineering Marvels
reading.text: The pyramids of Egypt, built over 4,500 years ago, remain a source of wonder. The Great Pyramid of Giza, originally 146 meters tall, was constructed from over 2 million stone blocks, each weighing an average of 2.5 tons. How ancient Egyptians transported and lifted these blocks without modern machinery is still debated. The most accepted theory involves ramps and a large workforce of skilled laborers, not slaves as once thought. Recent discoveries of workers' tombs and dietary records suggest that the pyramid builders were well-fed and highly organized.

reading.title: The Microbiome: Trillions of Tiny Allies
reading.text: The human body is home to trillions of microorganisms, collectively called the microbiome. These bacteria, fungi, and viruses live on our skin, in our mouths, and especially in our intestines. Far from being harmful, most of them are beneficial. They help digest food, produce vitamins, and train our immune system. Disruption of the microbiome through antibiotics or poor diet has been linked to allergies, obesity, and even mental health issues. Researchers are now exploring how to restore a healthy microbiome through probiotics and personalized medicine.
